messages:
maria_ops: FYI vendor just flagged a tariff reclassification on returns — customs in FRA reclassifying our RMA units as 'used goods', which is triggering a higher duty + longer clearance. vendor says this affects returns and replacements shipped from EU forwarders :grimacing:

tony_procure: ugh. do we have an immediate delta on landed cost if they apply duties to returns? ballpark numbers suffice for the exec ask.

vendor_bot: Vendor notice: FRA customs update effective 2025-11-12. Impact: potential +12-18% duty on returned/refurb units. Contact vendor-reclaims@thirdpartylogi.co for disputed classifications.

maria_ops: vendor gave two options: 1) standard RMA return (subject to duty + delay) or 2) salvage/refurb route — vendor keeps defective units locally, issues refurbished replacements as new shipments (lower duty, but vendor wants a salvage credit and warranty carveout).

anya_logistics: salvage route saves ~3-5 business days on clearance and avoids return AWB costs. downside: vendor wants 20% credit on net unit price and 30-day limited warranty instead of full 12mo. Need to confirm serial reconciliation process and disposition proof (photos + test logs).

kai_sre: cluster impact: if we lose 24 H100s from EU pool for 2wks that's ~22% throughput hit on eu-dedicated-1. We should trigger temporary routing -> eu-hosted-fallback and prioritize latency-sensitive customers. Ops must tell product which customers get degraded.

tony_procure: numbers: typical H100 landed unit cost \u20ac52k. 20% salvage credit -> \u20ac10.4k back to us, but risk-in-warranty reduces our TCO if refurb fail rate >8%. With +12-18% duty on returns, a straight RMA return could cost up to \u20ac9k/duty per unit. Salvage might be cheaper overall depending on refurb repro rate.

maria_ops: request: vendor provide sample manifest and proof-of-destruction/refurb workflow. we also need AWB reuse vs new AWB cost delta. can you push vendor for a pilot 10-unit workflow and reduced credit (15%)?

vendor_bot: Vendor update: can do 10-unit pilot, provisional salvage credit 15% for pilot, requires signed MOU and disposition SLA. Pilot ETA: dispatch replacements in 5 business days after MOU + serial manifest.

anya_logistics: sample manifest (CSV snippet):
``
serial,model,status,received_date,photo_url,test_log
H100-XY12345,H100,defective,2025-11-01,https://img.thirdparty/xy.jpg,log_1234.txt
H100-XY12346,H100,defective,2025-11-02,https://img.thirdparty/xy2.jpg,log_1235.txt
```

maria_ops: good. also need chain-of-custody and clear insured value for replacements. if vendor ships refurbished as 'new' customs will still inspect. include invoice language: "replacement units — declared value \u20ac0 for returned defective cores" is risky. 

kai_sre: ops-side mitigations: we can spin up short-term cloud fallbacks and enable aggressive batching to reduce load. But we need traffic routing doc for product and SREs by EOD so they can notify customers.

tony_procure: I'll do cost sim for both flows (RMA vs salvage pilot) and include depreciation+failure risk. ETA: 12:00 UTC tomorrow.

maria_ops: action items: 1) tony -> detailed cost sim (due 12:00 UTC) 2) anya -> confirm crossdock window + AWB delta and pilot paperwork (due EOD today) 3) vendor -> send MOU draft and sample disposition SLA 4) kai -> routing playbook draft.

ops_escalations: escalations note: tagging legal and compliance for MOU review once vendor shares. cc: legal@redwood.com :email:

maria_ops: thanks team. if pilot sounds OK we'll accept 10-unit to validate salvage path. will post updates here. :shipit:
